title: The truncation couple is an exact couple
statement:
Let $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be left exact and additive
[def-sp-left-exact-additive] between Grothendieck abelian categories
[def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], and let $K\in\operatorname{Ch}^+(\mathcal A)$
be bounded below with $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q<a$. Then the truncation
couple [def-sp-truncation-couple] of $K$, with the structure maps $\alpha$,
$f$, $g$ of bidegrees $(-1,+1)$, $(+2,-1)$, $(0,0)$ of
[def-sp-truncation-couple], is an exact couple [def-sp-exact-couple].

proof.text:
**Step 1 (the structure maps, read off the triangles).** For $q\in\mathbf Z$ let $T_q:\ \tau_{\leq q-1}K\xrightarrow{i_q}\tau_{\leq q}K\xrightarrow{j_q}\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]\xrightarrow{k_q}(\tau_{\leq q-1}K)[1]$ be the truncation triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] ($i_q$ the inclusion of canonical truncations, $j_q$ the projection $\Ker d^q_K\to\mathcal H^q(K)$ in degree $q$, $k_q$ the unique third map making $T_q$ distinguished in $D(\mathcal A)$); these are the triangles named in [def-sp-truncation-couple]. Since $K$ is bounded below, so are $\tau_{\leq q-1}K$, $\tau_{\leq q}K$ and $\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]$, so $T_q$ lies in $D^+(\mathcal A)$. With $D^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rv\,\tau_{\leq q}K)$ and $E^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rv(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]))$, the only maps between these objects that $T_q$ and $T_{q+1}$ provide with the bidegrees prescribed in [def-sp-truncation-couple] are
$$\alpha=\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rv\,i_{q+1}):D^{p,q}\to D^{p-1,q+1},\qquad g=\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rv\,j_q):D^{p,q}\to E^{p,q},$$
$$f:E^{p,q}\xrightarrow{\ \mathcal H^{p+q}(\sigma_{\tau_{\leq q-1}K}\circ Rv\,k_q)\ }\mathcal H^{p+q}\bigl((Rv\,\tau_{\leq q-1}K)[1]\bigr)=\mathcal H^{p+q+1}(Rv\,\tau_{\leq q-1}K)=D^{p+2,q-1},$$
with $\sigma$ the shift isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated] and $\mathcal H^{n}(M[1])=\mathcal H^{n+1}(M)$ the literal equality of subquotients for the convention $(M[1])^r=M^{r+1}$, $d_{M[1]}=-d_M$ (negating the differential changes neither its kernel nor its image). Bidegree check: $\tau_{\leq q}K$ has $D$-index $q$, total degree $p+q$ is kept by $\alpha$ and $g$, so $\alpha$ lands in $\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rv\,\tau_{\leq q+1}K)=D^{p-1,q+1}$, i.e. bidegree $(-1,+1)$, and $g$ has bidegree $(0,0)$; $f$ raises the total degree by one and lowers $q$ by one, so it lands in $D^{p',q-1}$ with $p'+q-1=p+q+1$, $p'=p+2$, bidegree $(+2,-1)$. This $f$ is the boundary named in [def-sp-truncation-couple]. Here $Rv$ is applied to the morphism $k_q$ of $D^+(\mathcal A)$, which is not a chain map: so $Rv$ must be the functor on $D^+(\mathcal A)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated], which on objects is the $Rv$ of [def-sp-kinjective-bridge] ($v$ applied to a K-injective resolution; any two choices canonically isomorphic and the construction functorial, [lem-sp-kinjective-computes] (1)), and which exists because a Grothendieck abelian category has enough injectives [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. The hypothesis $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q<a$ is not used anywhere in this proof.

source.place: Remark 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle, line 4076; the triangle tau_{<=a}K -> tau_{<=a+1}K -> H^{a+1}(K)[-a-1] -> (tau_{<=a}K)[1] at line 4101, here a=q-1); Proposition 05SE (proposition-derived-functor, line 4895) and Lemma 05SU (lemma-derived-shift) for Rv on D^+ and its shift isomorphism

proof.text:
**Step 2 (the image triangles are distinguished).** By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated], applied to $v$ (additive, left exact, $\mathcal A$ with enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]) and to the distinguished triangle $T_q$ of $D^+(\mathcal A)$ (Step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle]), the triangle
$$Rv(T_q):\quad Rv\,\tau_{\leq q-1}K\xrightarrow{Rv\,i_q}Rv\,\tau_{\leq q}K\xrightarrow{Rv\,j_q}Rv(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q])\xrightarrow{\sigma_{\tau_{\leq q-1}K}\circ Rv\,k_q}(Rv\,\tau_{\leq q-1}K)[1]$$
is distinguished in $D^+(\mathcal B)$, hence in $D(\mathcal B)$ ($D^+(\mathcal B)$ being a full triangulated subcategory).

source.place: Proposition 05SE (proposition-derived-functor, line 4895), parts (2) and (7): a right derived functor is exact on the triangulated subcategory where it is defined

proof.text:
**Step 3 (the long exact sequence, and its connecting map is $f$).** Apply the long exact cohomology sequence of a distinguished triangle of $D(\mathcal B)$ [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] to $Rv(T_q)$ (Step 2). With $n=p+q$ it reads
$$\cdots\to\mathcal H^{n}(Rv\,\tau_{\leq q-1}K)\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^n(Rv\,i_q)}\mathcal H^{n}(Rv\,\tau_{\leq q}K)\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^n(Rv\,j_q)}\mathcal H^{n}(Rv(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]))\xrightarrow{\ \delta^n\ }\mathcal H^{n+1}(Rv\,\tau_{\leq q-1}K)\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^{n+1}(Rv\,i_q)}\mathcal H^{n+1}(Rv\,\tau_{\leq q}K)\to\cdots$$
exact at every spot. Its connecting map is, as in Stacks (0148: the map $H^0(Z)\to H^1(X)$ is $H(h)$ with $H^1(X)=H(X[1])$, 'we will not use any signs') and in the Mathlib match of [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] (`DerivedCategory.HomologySequence.δ T n₀ n₁ h := (homologyFunctor C 0).shiftMap T.mor₃ n₀ n₁ _`), $\mathcal H^n$ of the third map of the triangle followed by the identification $\mathcal H^n(M[1])=\mathcal H^{n+1}(M)$; for $Rv(T_q)$ that is $\delta^n=\mathcal H^{n}(\sigma\circ Rv\,k_q)$, which is $f:E^{p,q}\to D^{p+2,q-1}$ of Step 1. In the notation of Step 1 the sequence is
$$\cdots\to D^{p+1,q-1}\xrightarrow{\ \alpha\ }D^{p,q}\xrightarrow{\ g\ }E^{p,q}\xrightarrow{\ f\ }D^{p+2,q-1}\xrightarrow{\ \alpha\ }D^{p+1,q}\to\cdots$$
(the first map is $\alpha=\mathcal H^{(p+1)+(q-1)}(Rv\,i_q)$ out of $D^{p+1,q-1}$, the last $\alpha=\mathcal H^{(p+2)+(q-1)}(Rv\,i_q)$ out of $D^{p+2,q-1}$). Sign conventions: other conventions in the literature put a sign $\pm1$ (depending on $n$, or on the rotation used, cf. the remark after 0148) on the connecting map or on the identification $\mathcal H^n(M[1])\cong\mathcal H^{n+1}(M)$; this replaces $f$ by $\pm f$ in each bidegree, which changes neither $\Ker f$ nor $\operatorname{im}f$, so nothing below depends on the convention. (The same sequence is what [lem-sp-long-exact-of-triangle] gives for the homological functor $\mathcal H^0:D(\mathcal B)\to\mathcal B$, Stacks 05RS; the Mathlib leaf [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] is used instead because it needs no node for '$\mathcal H^0$ is homological'.)

source.place: Definition 0147 (definition-homological, line 261) and the long exact sequence 0148 (equation-long-exact-cohomology-sequence, line 281, 'we will not use any signs'); Lemma 05RS (lemma-cohomology-homological, line 3618) and the sequence equation-long-exact-cohomology-sequence-D (line 3640)

proof.text: **Step 4 (the three identities of an exact couple).** Exactness of the sequence of Step 3 (for the triangle $T_q$) at $D^{p,q}$ is $\Ker(g:D^{p,q}\to E^{p,q})=\operatorname{im}(\alpha:D^{p+1,q-1}\to D^{p,q})$, and at $E^{p,q}$ it is $\Ker(f:E^{p,q}\to D^{p+2,q-1})=\operatorname{im}(g:D^{p,q}\to E^{p,q})$. Exactness of the sequence of Step 3 for the triangle $T_{q+1}$, at its spot $\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rv\,\tau_{\leq q}K)=D^{p,q}$ (the term $\mathcal H^{n+1}(Rv\,\tau_{\leq (q+1)-1}K)$ with $n=p+q-1$), is $\Ker(\alpha:D^{p,q}\to D^{p-1,q+1})=\operatorname{im}(f:E^{p-2,q+1}\to D^{p,q})$, since $E^{p-2,q+1}=\mathcal H^{p+q-1}(Rv(\mathcal H^{q+1}(K)[-q-1]))$. These are the three identities of [def-sp-exact-couple] at $(p,q)$; the inclusions $\operatorname{im}\subseteq\Ker$ among them are the vanishing of the composites of two consecutive structure maps also required there. As $p,q\in\mathbf Z$ are arbitrary, $(D,E,\alpha,f,g)$ is an exact couple.

source.place: Section 12.21 (011P), Definition 011Q (definition-exact-couple, line 5289): Ker(alpha)=Im(f), Ker(f)=Im(g), Ker(g)=Im(alpha); bigraded with the bidegrees of def-sp-exact-couple

split_report.summary: Statement kept. The one-step imported proof is split into four steps. Step 1 reads the structure maps off def-sp-truncation-couple (which names only f and the bidegrees): alpha = H^{p+q}(Rv i_{q+1}), g = H^{p+q}(Rv j_q), f = H^{p+q}(sigma o Rv k_q) followed by H^n(M[1]) = H^{n+1}(M), with the bidegrees (-1,+1), (0,0), (+2,-1) checked; it cites the truncation triangle lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle (silent in def-sp-truncation-couple) and notes that Rv must be the functor on D^+ of lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated (k_q is not a chain map), equal on objects to the Rv of def-sp-kinjective-bridge, defined since Grothendieck categories have enough injectives. Step 2: Rv(T_q) distinguished (lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated, Lean closed). Step 3: the long exact sequence by the Mathlib leaf lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact (replacing lem-sp-long-exact-of-triangle, which would need a node for 'H^0 is homological'); its connecting map is H^n of the third map (Stacks 0148, no signs; Mathlib HomologySequence.δ = shiftMap of mor₃), i.e. f; sign conventions only change f by a unit. Step 4: the three identities of def-sp-exact-couple, the first one from the sequence of T_{q+1}, the other two from that of T_q (the imported text put all three at bidegree (p,q) of one sequence, which is off by one for ker alpha = im f). The hypothesis H^q(K)=0 for q<a is unused. Same argument as Step 2 of lem-weil-pbc-truncation-couple-morphism (for Phi = g^{-1}Rf_*, Psi = Rf'_*g'^{-1}); not duplicated. Not in Mathlib (no exact couples; three kinds of search recorded). No new nodes.

reviewed.note: the off-by-one of the imported proof corrected (ker α = im f comes from the sequence of T_{q+1}); lem-sp-kinjective-computes and lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives (sk-prop-av-pqf-finite) accepted as tool uses; lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact is a Mathlib leaf

lean.statement: theorem truncationCouple_exact {A : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} A] [Abelian A] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v₁} A] {B : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} B] [Abelian B] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v₂} B] (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F] (K : CochainComplex.Plus A) (a : ℤ) (ha : ∀ q : ℤ, q < a → IsZero (K.obj.homology q)) : (∀ p q : ℤ, ∃ w : (truncationCouple F K a ha).2.2.2.1 p q ≫ (truncationCouple F K a ha).2.2.1 (p + 2) (q - 1) = 0, (ShortComplex.mk _ _ w).Exact) ∧ (∀ p q : ℤ, ∃ w : (truncationCouple F K a ha).2.2.2.2 p q ≫ (truncationCouple F K a ha).2.2.2.1 p q = 0, (ShortComplex.mk _ _ w).Exact) ∧ (∀ p q : ℤ, ∃ w : (truncationCouple F K a ha).2.2.1 p q ≫ (truncationCouple F K a ha).2.2.2.2 (p - 1) (q + 1) = 0, (ShortComplex.mk _ _ w).Exact)

reviewed_lean.note: A,B Grothendieck abelian (IsGrothendieckAbelian, indep. universes); v additive+left exact = F.Additive+PreservesFiniteLimits; K : CochainComplex.Plus A; a, ha vanishing below a retained; conclusion: landed truncationCouple F K a ha components, zero composite + ShortComplex.Exact at D^{p+2,q-1} (f,alpha), E^{p,q} (g,f), D^{p-1,q+1} (alpha,g) for all p q in Z
